name: Juvenile Rukh, Mythic
body:
MYTHIC JUVENILE RUKH
CR 4/MR 1

XP 1,200
N Large magical beast (mythic)
Init +2; Senses low-light vision; Perception +17
Aura stench (DC 14, 5 rounds)

DEFENSE

AC 16, touch 11, flat-footed 14 (+2 Dex, +5 natural, -1 size)
hp 47 (5d10+20)
Fort +6, Ref +6, Will +2
DR 5/epic

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 40 ft. (poor)
Melee 2 bites +7 (1d8+2), 2 talons +6 (1d6+2 plus disease)
Space 10 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks mythic power (1/day, surge ++1d6)

STATISTICS

Str 14, Dex 15, Con 14, Int 2, Wis 13, Cha 11
Base Atk +5; CMB +8; CMD 20
Feats Flyby Attack, Snatch, Weapon Focus (bite)
Skills Fly -4, Perception +17; Racial Modifiers +8 Perception

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Filth Fever (Ex)

Talons—injury; save Fort DC 14, onset 1d3 days, frequency 1 day, effect 1d3 Dex damage, 1d3 Con damage, cure 2 consecutive saves.

ECOLOGY

Environment warm deserts or mountains
Organization pair or flock (3d4)
Treasure incidental

Rukhs are foul-tempered creatures resembling two-headed vultures, relatives of the majestic rocs. Unlike their raptor cousins, rukhs have a sinister appearance and thrive on both live prey and carrion. They glide over deserts, scanning for easy targets like horses, camels, and humanoids, though they avoid creatures of their size or larger. Rukhs nest in mountainous regions or cliffside caves, far from potential threats. Despite their size, adult rukhs are often scrawny, driven by near-constant hunger. Their young are frequently hunted by desert tribes for food, often lured into ambushes by deceptive scouts. A typical adult rukh stands nearly 35 feet tall, with a wingspan exceeding 60 feet, yet weighs less than 800 pounds due to its lightweight bones.

Juveniles. A juvenile rukh is a massive bird of prey with feathers that shimmer like gold in the sunlight. Though not yet fully grown, these majestic creatures are fierce predators, known to soar over vast landscapes in search of prey.

They are revered in some cultures as omens of power and good fortune, while others fear their predatory nature and territorial aggression.
